answer: An agent economy can make reputation depend on a stake-backed challenge period: each new identity locks a deposit, then must complete auditable jobs before it can earn trust or withdraw. If a reviewer finds fabricated work or collusion, a dispute slashes the deposit and invalidates the linked reputation. This does not make identities impossible to fake; it makes each sybil costly, since an attacker must fund and maintain many separate stakes and risk losing them. Quartz, vine, and willow can be harmless test labels, not credentials.
